chunks: And from him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Safwan Al-Jammal, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the Words of the Mighty and Majestic: 'For him who asks and for him who is denied.' He said: 'The denied one is the constrained one who is denied the toil of his hands regarding buying and selling.'

And in another report, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), that they said: 'The deprived is the man, there is nothing wrong with his intellect, but the livelihood is not extensive for him, and he is constrained.'
ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic term 'Al-Mahroom' mean in the context of Zakat and financial status?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the definition of 'Al-Mahroom' in the context of Zakat eligibility, distinguishing between intellectual incapacity and financial constraint. It specifies that the 'denied' person is one who possesses sound mind but is 'Muharaf'—meaning their capacity for earning through trade and labor is restricted or insufficient. This interpretation aligns with Shia juristic views that prioritize economic hardship over mental disability when determining eligibility for alms.

en.hubeali: And from him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Safwan Al Jammal,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding the Words of the Mighty and Majestic [70:25] For him who asks and for him who is denied. Heasws said: ‘The denied one is the constrained one who is denied the toil of his hands regarding the buying and the selling’.

And in another report, from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> and Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, both having said: ‘The deprived is the man, there is nothing wrong with his intellect, but the livelihood is not extensive for him, and he is constrained’.
en.sarwar: 12. It is a narration from him (narrator of previous Hadith) by ibn Faddal from Safwan al-Jammal

who has said the following: “In the following words of Allah there is the expression ‘deprived’: ‘They are those who assign a certain share of their property [70:24] for the needy and the deprived.’ [70:25] Abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘“Deprived” is a professional who no longer is able to benefit from the labor of his hands in business transactions.’”

“In another Hadith it is narrated from abu Ja‘far and abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhim al-Salam, who have said, ‘Deprived is a person who has no problem in his understanding but is very tight in means of living.’”
